reason: The narrative is told from a third-person omniscient perspective focused primarily on leaders and divine communication. The main characters and narrative focus are: (1) God issuing commands, (2) Moses as the central mediator, (3) Aaron as the high priest, (4) Joshua and Caleb as tribal leaders, and (5) the twelve spies (all described as leaders/chiefs of their tribes). While the Israelite congregation is present as respondents and complainers, the story is not told from their perspective or viewpoint. It is a historical account structured around leadership decisions, divine judgment, and high-level interactions between God and leaders, not an account from the standpoint of ordinary laborers or working-class people.
